This is accomplished by the agency’s commitment to “The PCHAS Way” which inspires the agency to be strength-focused, family-centered, and goal driven with every client.

Benefits of serving children and families in need through PCHAS include competitive salaries, flex work schedules, paid time off, medical, dental and vision insurance options, voluntary life insurance options, paid holidays, and a very generous retirement plan (after one year of service and working 1,000 hours the agency matches an employee 200% up to a 3%.

FLSA Status:
Non-Exempt

This position is a 6-month temporary assignment with the potential for permanent employment based on business needs, performance, workload, and overall fit. Employment is at-will, meaning either the employee or the agency may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, in accordance with applicable law.

This position is going to be roughly 20 hours a week.

Position Summary

We are seeking a dependable, compassionate, and flexible individual to serve as an Assistant Case Manager
supporting children and families participating in the Foster Care Case Management (FCCM) program
.

The Assistant Case Manager will work under the direction of the assigned Foster Care Case Manager or Supervisor to provide essential support to children and families throughout their involvement with the program. Responsibilities may include transportation, supervised visitation, documentation, communication with families and service providers, and other case management support as needed.

The ideal candidate will be dependable, patient, observant, organized, and able to build positive and professional relationships with children, families, and community partners. The ability to maintain confidentiality, establish appropriate boundaries, follow safety procedures, and remain professional in a variety of settings is essential.

This position is ideal for someone who is passionate about supporting children and families, comfortable working independently, and able to adapt to changing client needs and schedules. The Assistant Case Manager will play an important role in helping ensure children and families receive consistent, safe, and supportive services throughout the FCCM process.

Essential Job Functions

Provide supervised visitation for children and their parents/families in accordance with case plans and agency requirements.
Safely transport children and clients to and from supervised visits, foster care placements, medical appointments, school, and other approved activities.
Travel throughout the state as required to meet the needs of children and families.
Monitor parent-child interactions during supervised visitation and provide appropriate support and guidance.
Address and reinforce positive parenting skills during supervised visits.
Promote positive parenting practices, healthy family relationships, and appropriate child development.
Support efforts to reduce the risk of child maltreatment by modeling and reinforcing safe and appropriate parenting behaviors.
Maintain accurate, thorough, and timely documentation regarding transportation, visitation, client interactions, and other services provided.
Communicate observations, concerns, and relevant information to the assigned Foster Care Case Manager or Supervisor.
Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality when working with children, families, foster parents, and other service providers.
Establish and maintain positive, respectful, and professional relationships with children and families.
Observe and report changes in a child's behavior, circumstances, or needs to the appropriate Case Manager or Supervisor.
Follow all agency policies, safety procedures, case plans, and applicable requirements related to working with children and families.
Assist the assigned Case Manager with administrative and case-related tasks as needed.
Coordinate with foster parents, biological parents, schools, healthcare providers, service providers, and other approved individuals as directed.
Provide reliable and consistent support to children and families throughout their participation in the FCCM program.
Maintain accurate records and protect confidential and sensitive client information at all times.
Perform other duties related to the support of the FCCM program as assigned.

Working Conditions

This temporary position may involve working in a variety of environments depending on the needs of the children and families served. Assignments may take place in offices, homes, foster homes, residential facilities, hospitals, schools, court-related settings, and other community locations.

The Position May Require

Working days, evenings, nights, weekends, holidays, and/or extended hours based on program and client needs.
Driving regularly throughout various geographic and community settings.
Traveling extensively throughout the state as required.
Safely transporting children and clients in accordance with agency policies and applicable requirements.
Sitting, standing, bending, reaching, walking, and other routine physical activity.
Lifting and carrying items weighing up to 25 pounds.
Using computers, telephones, copiers, calculators, and other standard office equipment.
Maintaining alertness and attentiveness while supervising children and interacting with families.
Remaining professional, patient, and composed when working with children, families, foster parents, and individuals experiencing challenging circumstances.
Working independently while also following direction from Foster Care Case Managers and Supervisors.
Maintaining confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries in all work environments.
Adapting to changing schedules, locations, and client needs while maintaining dependable and consistent service.

Requirements

High School Diploma or GED equivalent required.
Valid driver's license required for assignments involving transportation.
Reliable transportation and ability to travel as required.
Ability to work effectively with children, parents, foster families, clients, facility staff, and other professionals.
Strong observation, communication, organization, and documentation skills.
Ability to remain calm, attentive, and professional in potentially challenging situations.
Ability to follow written and verbal instructions, safety procedures, agency policies, and facility guidelines.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries.
Ability to remain engaged and attentive throughout an assigned shift.
Ability to adapt to changing schedules, assignments, and client needs.
Ability to safely transport clients when transportation duties are assigned.
Ability to work independently while appropriately communicating concerns and observations to supervisors or designated staff.

Preferred Experience

Prior experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred but may not be required:

Foster care or child welfare
Case management or case management support
Social services
Working with children and families
Supervised visitation
Family support services
Child and family advocacy
Community-based services
Youth services or mentoring
Transportation services involving children or families
Residential or foster care settings
Documentation and case-related administrative support
Crisis intervention or conflict resolution
Experience working with individuals from diverse backgrounds

Candidates may be considered based on their overall experience, qualifications, reliability, communication skills, ability to work independently, and ability to effectively support children and families. Experience working in a child- or family-focused environment is preferred, but candidates with transferable skills and a demonstrated commitment to supporting children and families may also be considered.

Other Requirements

Must be dependable and consistently report for scheduled assignments.
Must be able to maintain confidentiality and protect sensitive client and family information.
Must maintain appropriate professional boundaries at all times.
Must comply with all applicable agency, facility, safety, and client-specific requirements.
Must be willing to complete any required onboarding, orientation, training, background screening, or other pre-employment requirements applicable to the assignment.
Must immediately communicate safety concerns, incidents, significant changes in client behavior or condition, and other relevant concerns to the appropriate staff member or supervisor.
Must perform only duties that are within the individual's training, authorization, and assigned responsibilities.

Temporary Contract Term

This is an approximately six month temporary contract position
. The initial assignment is expected to last approximately months; however, the contract may be extended based on the amount of work available, client needs, program needs, staffing requirements, and organizational needs
.

The selected individuals should be comfortable with the possibility that assignments and hours may vary throughout the contract period.

Christian Commitment

Presbyterian Children’s Homes and Services (PCHAS) is a faith-based organization guided by Christ’s love, dedicated to creating a world where every child is safe, every family is strong, and hope outshines hardship.

Through Christ-centered care, we empower children, young adults, and families by nurturing their strengths, resilience, and faith. We strive to serve like Jesus—meeting those we serve where they are, treating them with dignity and compassion, and walking alongside them with grace and understanding.

At PCHAS, we focus on the strengths and potential within each individual, encouraging those we serve to look forward with hope and confidence rather than being defined by past challenges. When we live out this mission well, we help children and families experience hope, thrive in their journeys, and know the enduring love of God.
